title: Desk admin sets ticket types, templates and status labels
story: As a desk admin, I want ticket types, templates and our own status names, so that each kind of work has the right form and flow.
acceptance: Given incident, service request and question types, then each has its own form and status flow.
Given a ticket of the wrong type, when an agent converts it, then its history stays and SLA targets restart under the new type.
Given a template, when an agent or rule applies it, then fields are filled, required or hidden fields are set and its checklist is added.
Given a custom status label, then it maps to one fixed system state (new, open, pending, on hold, solved) so SLA pause and reports still work.

title: Agent uses saved views, boards and bulk actions
story: As an agent, I want my own views and actions on many tickets at once, so that I clear the queue fast.
acceptance: Given the list, then I choose columns, filters and sort, also on custom fields, and save views as personal or shared.
Given the board view, when I drag a card, then its status changes and work-in-progress limits are shown.
Given many selected tickets, when I assign, change status or priority, tag, merge or close, then it applies to all and each change is audited.
Given a saved scenario, when I run it on one or many tickets, then all its field changes, note and reply are applied together.
Given a search, when I export it, then the CSV holds only tickets and fields I may see.

title: Agent sees requester context beside the ticket
story: As an agent, I want the requester's history and assets next to the ticket, so that I do not ask what we already know.
acceptance: Given a ticket, then a side panel shows the requester's other open and recent tickets, their assets and CIs.
Given the ticket text, then similar incidents and matching known errors are listed.
Given several tickets, then I can keep them open as tabs.
Given sensitive tickets of the requester in another queue, then they are not shown to me (YX-HD-03).

title: Watchers, VIPs and tickets raised for someone else
story: As a requester, I want to add colleagues, raise tickets for others and have VIPs flagged, so that the right people stay informed.
acceptance: Given a ticket, then requesters and agents can add watchers who get updates; people in CC of an incoming email are added automatically.
Given a watcher, then they are marked internal-only or external, and internal-only watchers never see private notes.
Given a ticket raised for someone else, then it keeps 'opened by' and 'requested for', and both can follow it.
Given a VIP requester, then the ticket is flagged and its priority or routing rule for VIPs applies.

title: Agent uses side conversations and splits tickets
story: As an agent, I want separate threads with other teams or vendors inside the ticket, so that the requester sees only what is meant for them.
acceptance: Given a ticket, when I start a side conversation by email, Teams / Slack or a child ticket, then replies stay attached to the ticket.
Given a side conversation, then the requester never sees it.
Given one message in a ticket, when I choose "new ticket", then a linked ticket is made from it.
Given a ticket with two issues, when I split it, then two linked tickets exist with their own SLAs.

title: Agent adds tasks to incidents and keeps standalone tasks
story: As an agent, I want tasks inside incidents and on their own, so that all small work is tracked.
acceptance: Given an incident, then I add tasks with assignee, due date and status.
Given open tasks, then the incident cannot be resolved until they are done or cancelled.
Given a task with no ticket, then it shows in a task list with its own status and due date.

title: Agent closes with resolution codes and escalates by support level
story: As a team lead, I want resolution codes and clear L1 / L2 / L3 steps, so that reports show how tickets are solved.
acceptance: Given a resolve action, then a resolution code and a resolution note are required.
Given an escalation from L1 to L2 or L3, then the step, time and reason are recorded.
Given reports, then they count tickets by resolution code and by level that solved them.

title: Desk admin sets reopen rules and requesters open a follow-up
story: As a desk admin, I want reopen rules per desk, so that old tickets are handled fairly.
acceptance: Given a desk or category, then I set who may reopen, from which states and for how many days.
Given the reopen window has passed, when the requester replies, then a follow-up ticket is made and linked to the closed one.
Given the default, then the 7-day rule of YX-HD-05 applies (YX-HD-05).

title: Agent sets reminders, snoozes tickets and sees a personal calendar
story: As an agent, I want reminders, snooze and my own calendar, so that I follow up on time.
acceptance: Given a ticket, then I set a reminder and get notified at that time.
Given snooze until a date, then the ticket leaves my queue view until then and comes back by itself.
Given my calendar, then it shows my tasks, changes, reminders and time off and has an iCal feed.

title: Agent writes rich replies and tags tickets
story: As an agent, I want rich replies and tags, so that answers are clear and tickets are easy to find.
acceptance: Given the editor, then I can drag in several files, paste inline images and embed a video link.
Given tags, then I add free tags to a ticket and use them in filters, rules and reports.
Given a pasted file, then it goes through the same virus scan as email attachments.

title: Assignment skips agents who are away, on leave or off shift
story: As a team lead, I want automatic assignment to respect leave and shifts, so that tickets do not wait with absent agents.
acceptance: Given an agent on approved leave in YukthiX HR or marked out of office, then round-robin and load-based assignment skip them.
Given shift hours, then an agent outside their shift gets no new tickets.
Given an agent, then they can set their own away status and time off.
Given the team view, then the lead sees who is available now.

title: Desk admin runs several SLA targets on one ticket
story: As a desk admin, I want several targets on one ticket, so that every promise is measured.
acceptance: Given a policy, then it can set time to assign, first response, next response after each requester message, and resolution.
Given a custom measure (time with vendor, time to approve), then it can have its own target.
Given a ticket, then each target shows its own due time and state.

title: SLA policy has its own conditions and business hours
story: As a desk admin, I want start, pause and stop conditions and hours per policy, so that SLAs fit how each team works.
acceptance: Given a policy, then pause can depend on any field (for example 'waiting for part').
Given a policy attached late, then the clock can count from ticket creation.
Given a policy, then it has its own business hours and uses the requester's, team's or site's time zone.
Given scope rules, then they combine any fields with AND / OR.

title: SLA milestones run actions at any percentage
story: As a team lead, I want actions at chosen points of the SLA, so that we act early.
acceptance: Given milestones such as 50, 75, 100 and 150 %, then each can have several actions (notify, reassign, raise priority, run a rule).
Given each target, then it can have its own milestones.
Given a milestone fires, then the action is logged on the ticket (YX-HD-02).

title: Lead tracks period compliance targets and breach reasons
story: As a team lead, I want monthly compliance targets and reasons for breaches, so that reports are fair.
acceptance: Given a target like '95 % of P2 solved in 8 h each month', then the report shows progress and an at-risk warning during the month.
Given a breach, then the agent must give a reason.
Given an exclusion approved by the lead, then the ticket is left out of SLA counts and the decision is audited.

title: Agent sees the SLA timeline on the ticket
story: As an agent, I want a picture of the SLA clock, so that I understand why time ran or stopped.
acceptance: Given a ticket, then a timeline shows running, paused and breached parts per target.
Given a pause, then the reason (status or condition) is shown.
Given the requester view, then only the due time is shown, not internal reasons.

title: Company sends desk email from its own domain and mailbox
story: As a desk admin, I want our own mailbox and sending domain, so that emails come from us and reach the inbox.
acceptance: Given Microsoft 365 or Gmail, then the mailbox connects by OAuth for receiving and sending; SMTP / IMAP is also possible.
Given a sending domain, then a wizard shows the SPF, DKIM and DMARC records and checks them.
Given bounces, then the admin can see and clear the bounce list for desk addresses.
Given a failed check, then sending falls back to our address and the admin is told.

title: Desk admin filters and parses incoming email
story: As a desk admin, I want rules on incoming email, so that tickets arrive sorted and filled.
acceptance: Given a filter on sender, domain, subject, header or pattern, then the email is routed, tagged, prioritised or rejected before it becomes a ticket.
Given parsing rules (key: value lines or patterns), then values are copied into ticket fields.
Given an address, then it can have a default template.

title: Requester gets an acknowledgement and replies with commands
story: As a requester, I want an instant receipt and simple reply commands, so that I know my ticket number and can act by email.
acceptance: Given a new email ticket, then an acknowledgement per team goes out with the number and suggested articles (YX-HD-04).
Given a reply with a keyword such as 'close' or 'approve', then the ticket is updated if the sender is allowed.
Given an agent reply with field keywords, then status, priority or assignee change.
Given an unknown command, then nothing changes and the sender gets a short help reply.

title: Agents post known-issue banners with a 'me too' button
story: As an agent, I want banners for known issues and maintenance, so that people do not raise the same ticket again.
acceptance: Given a banner, then it shows on the portal and help drawer for the chosen audience or location.
Given 'me too', then the requester is linked to the open incident instead of making a new ticket.
Given a major incident, then a banner can be posted from it and ends when it is resolved.

title: Public can raise tickets through an open portal safely
story: As a desk admin, I want an open portal for people without an account, so that the public can ask for help without abuse.
acceptance: Given open portal mode, then a person submits with an email address and confirms by a link.
Given a submission, then a bot check and per-sender rate limits apply.
Given sign-up settings, then only allowed email domains can self-register, or sign-up is by invite only.

title: Portal shows our look, my time zone and reading aids
story: As a requester, I want a portal that looks like my company and fits my needs, so that it is easy to use.
acceptance: Given branding, then the login screen shows the company image and text and the portal uses its theme.
Given my profile, then all dates and SLA times show in my time zone and locale.
Given reading aids, then I can switch on a dyslexia-friendly font, reading mask, zoom and focus highlight.

title: Agent links articles in replies and flags outdated ones
story: As an agent, I want to insert articles and flag bad ones from the ticket, so that knowledge stays used and correct.
acceptance: Given a reply, then I insert an article link in one click.
Given a resolved ticket, then it records which article solved it and the article reuse count goes up.
Given an outdated article, when I flag it, then the author gets a task.
Given an article, then authors see a health score from use, feedback and flags.

title: Knowledge lead sees content gaps from searches
story: As a knowledge lead, I want a list of searches with no answer, so that we write the articles people need.
acceptance: Given searches with no result or no click, then they are grouped by topic in a report.
Given tickets closed without an article, then their topics are listed too.
Given a gap, then it can become an article-request task. Search terms stay without user ids (YX-GRO-07).

title: Author uses article templates and reusable blocks
story: As an author, I want templates and shared text blocks, so that articles are fast to write and easy to keep right.
acceptance: Given templates (how-to, troubleshooting, FAQ), then a new article starts from one.
Given a content block such as office address, when it changes, then every article using it shows the new text.
Given a category, then articles can be pinned or featured and carry video and files.

title: Desk keeps daily KPI snapshots with targets
story: As a team lead, I want KPIs stored every day with targets, so that I see trends that cannot be rebuilt later.
acceptance: Given the desk is live, then key KPIs are saved every day from day one.
Given a KPI, then it has a target and red / amber / green limits.
Given history, then trend lines and a simple forecast are shown.
Given a practice (incident, request, change), then a scorecard shows its KPIs.

title: Lead uses a ready report library and time-in-status reports
story: As a team lead, I want many ready reports, so that I do not build common reports myself.
acceptance: Given the library, then reports are grouped by practice (incident, request, change, asset, licence, SLA, agent).
Given an agent, group or requester, then a 360 report shows their tickets, times and ratings.
Given time-in-status, then I see time per status, team and approval step and where tickets get stuck or skip steps.

title: Team shows live boards on a wall screen
story: As a team lead, I want a live board for the team screen, so that everyone sees the queue.
acceptance: Given TV mode, then queue and SLA boards refresh by themselves full screen.
Given a threshold such as a backlog spike, then the lead gets an alert.
Given a wall screen, then it signs in with a view-only link that shows no ticket text.

title: Personal data in tickets is found and masked
story: As a requester, I want my ID numbers and passwords hidden in tickets, so that my data is safe.
acceptance: Given ticket text or custom fields with Aadhaar, PAN, bank, card, health data or passwords, then they are found and masked in the UI and audit.
Given AI calls, then masked values are never sent.
Given reveal rights, when a user unmasks, then the reveal is audited.
Given chosen custom fields, then they are encrypted at rest and shown only to allowed roles.

title: Admin sees who read what, with fuller audit detail
story: As a company admin, I want to see who viewed or searched tickets, so that misuse can be found.
acceptance: Given a ticket view, search or export, then who, what, when and from where is logged.
Given the audit, then it shows unset vs empty values and email events with CC.
Given the audit screen, then I filter by user, field and date.

title: Desk admin limits attachment file types
story: As a desk admin, I want a list of allowed file types, so that risky files never enter.
acceptance: Given an allow-list, then other file types are refused in portal, email and API (case-insensitive).
Given a refused file, then the sender is told why.
Given allowed files, then the virus scan still runs.

title: Standalone desk syncs users and groups from the directory
story: As an IT admin at a company without YukthiX HR, I want users and groups from our directory, so that the people list stays current.
acceptance: Given AD / LDAP, Entra ID or Google Workspace, then users and attributes (department, manager) sync on a schedule, on top of SCIM.
Given a directory group, then it can map to a desk team or role.
Given a disabled user, then their desk access ends.
Given rules or approvals, then they can look up a user's group membership (read only).

title: Collaborators join tickets without a full agent seat
story: As a desk admin, I want collaborators who help on tickets, so that experts can help without a full seat.
acceptance: Given the collaborator role, then the person can view tickets shared with them, add internal notes and work assigned tasks.
Given a collaborator, then they cannot own a ticket or reply to the requester.
Given billing, then collaborators are listed apart from agents and priced per the founder decision on collaborators.

title: New desk admin follows a guided set-up
story: As a new desk admin, I want a set-up checklist and wizard, so that the desk is ready in an hour.
acceptance: Given a new desk, then a wizard sets up queues, SLAs and the support email.
Given the checklist, then each step shows done or to do.
Given product updates, then a feed in the app shows what is new with help links.

title: Customer accounts, entitlements and company groups
Agent manages customer organisations and contacts
story: As an agent, I want customers grouped into organisations, so that I see the whole account.
acceptance: Given an organisation, then it has contacts, an account owner, sites and shared fields.
Given a contact, then they can belong to several organisations.
Given a customer admin contact, then they can see and follow all their organisation's tickets in the portal.
Given reports, then they can be cut by organisation.

title: Customer's support plan drives SLA and routing
story: As a team lead, I want support plans per customer, so that we give each customer what they bought.
acceptance: Given a plan, then it has tier, hours or tickets allowed, channels, SLA and expiry.
Given a ticket, then the plan shows on it and sets SLA and routing.
Given a plan near its end or used up, then the account owner is alerted and new tickets are flagged or held per the setting.

title: Company groups share settings with sub-companies
story: As a group IT head, I want sub-companies inside our company, so that one desk serves the whole group.
acceptance: Given a parent and sub-companies, then settings, rules and SLAs are inherited unless changed lower down.
Given an agent, then they can be limited to some sub-companies.
Given a requester, then they see only their own sub-company's catalogue and articles unless shared.

title: Tickets are tagged to products with their own KB and SLAs
story: As a support lead, I want tickets per product, so that each product team sees its work.
acceptance: Given products or modules, then tickets carry one.
Given a product, then it can have its own articles and SLA.
Given reports, then they can be cut by product.

title: Forms show, hide and require fields by earlier answers
story: As a desk admin, I want smart forms, so that requesters see only the questions that apply.
acceptance: Given form rules, then fields are shown, hidden, required, locked, defaulted or filtered by other answers, the requester profile or the item.
Given a questionnaire, then it can be reused in several items.
Given the company library, then shared fields, forms and rules are defined once and used by every desk, which can add its own.

title: Forms offer pickers for my assets, people and places
story: As a requester, I want to pick my device or cost centre from a list, so that I do not type wrong values.
acceptance: Given an asset picker, then I see only my own assets.
Given people, location, cost centre or CMDB pickers, then choices come from live data.
Given cascading fields, then the second list depends on the first.

title: Requester orders several items in one cart or through an order guide
story: As a requester, I want a cart and guided ordering, so that I ask once for all I need.
acceptance: Given the cart, then I add several items with quantities and options and check out once.
Given checkout, then each item gets its own approvals and tasks.
Given an order guide, when I answer a few questions (role, location), then the right items are added.
Given a request for someone else, then the cart is raised for them.

title: Catalogue pages are rich and requesters track stages
story: As a requester, I want clear item pages and a stage tracker, so that I know what I get and when.
acceptance: Given an item page, then it shows images, video, documents, delivery time and ratings.
Given my request, then I see stages: submitted, approval, fulfilment, delivered.
Given fulfilment has not started, then I can cancel.

title: Approvers act from chat cards and get reminders
story: As an approver, I want to approve from Teams, Slack or a push, so that requests are not stuck.
acceptance: Given an approval, then a Teams or Slack card and a mobile push let me approve or reject with a comment.
Given no answer, then reminders go at set intervals.
Given a timeout, then the request is auto-approved, auto-rejected or escalated per the item setting.
Given approved leave in YukthiX HR, then approvals go to my delegate (as in US-C-005).

title: Group approvals use a quorum
story: As a desk admin, I want group approvals with a quorum, so that committees decide properly.
acceptance: Given a group, then the rule is any one, all, N of M or a percentage.
Given the quorum reached, then the step closes and others are told.
Given a rejection rule, then one reject can stop the request if set.

title: Request creates documents and collects e-signatures
story: As an HR agent, I want documents made from templates inside a request, so that paperwork is done in the same flow.
acceptance: Given a template (hand-over form, NOC), then a document is made with request data (P05).
Given e-sign, then the person signs and the signed copy is stored on the request.
Given a signature still pending, then the request waits.

title: Agent moves or shares a ticket with another desk
story: As an agent, I want to hand over or share a ticket with another desk, so that it reaches the right team without losing context.
acceptance: Given a move to another desk, then fields are mapped and the new desk's privacy, SLA and category apply, with audit.
Given forwarding rules, then only allowed desk pairs can forward.
Given sharing, then the other team gets view, comment or full access while my team keeps ownership.
Given a sensitive ticket, then it can be moved only to a desk allowed to hold that category (YX-HD-03).

title: Desk admin clones a desk and delegates its admin
story: As a company admin, I want to copy a desk set-up and give its admin to the desk lead, so that new desks start fast and safely.
acceptance: Given a desk, then its set-up can be cloned into a new desk.
Given tickets or settings, then they can be moved between desks with audit.
Given a desk admin, then they can change only their own desk.

title: HR agent sees the employee summary beside a case
story: As an HR agent, I want the employee's basic HR facts beside the case, so that I help without switching screens.
acceptance: Given an HR case, then grade, manager, location and tenure show beside it.
Given hidden fields for my role, then they are not shown.
Given the standalone desk without HR, then the panel shows the light people list only.

title: Employee journeys coordinate transfers, promotions and leave
story: As an HR admin, I want journeys for life events, so that every team does its part on time.
acceptance: Given transfer, promotion, move, leave or return in M01, then a journey starts with tasks for HR, IT, Facilities, Payroll and Security.
Given variants by region, role or unit, then the right task set is used.
Given the journey tracker, then employee, manager and HR see where it stands.

title: Branches get their own hours, groups and admins
story: As a company admin, I want branch-level set-up, so that each site runs its own way.
acceptance: Given a site, then it has its own hours, holidays, groups, workflows and admins.
Given a requester's site, then tickets use that site's set-up.
Given a site admin, then they change only their site.

title: Admin installs automation recipes and traces rule runs
story: As a desk admin, I want ready recipes and a clear rule trace, so that automation is quick to set and easy to fix.
acceptance: Given the recipe library, then a recipe installs in one click as a draft rule.
Given a rule run, then the trace shows each condition, pass or fail and what changed.
Given run-count limits, then a rule over its limit stops and the admin is told.

title: Recurring tickets are created on a schedule
story: As a team lead, I want tickets made on a schedule, so that routine checks are never forgotten.
acceptance: Given a template and a pattern (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly), then tickets are created with assignee and SLA.
Given a run that was not created or not done, then it shows as missed.
Given a schedule, then it can be paused or ended.

title: Desk sends timed message sequences
story: As a desk admin, I want timed follow-up messages, so that requesters are reminded without manual work.
acceptance: Given a sequence, then it has steps with delays and messages.
Given the requester replies or the ticket closes, then the sequence stops.
Given notification preferences, then they are respected.

title: Agent asks for approval on any ticket; only the assignee completes tasks
story: As an agent, I want ad-hoc approvals and safe task completion, so that actions are approved and owned.
acceptance: Given any ticket, problem or task, then I can ask a named person to approve.
Given the answer, then it is recorded on the ticket.
Given a task or approval, then only its assignee or group can complete it, even if others can see it.

title: Agent follows a step-by-step runbook on the ticket
story: As an agent, I want runbooks on tickets, so that I follow the right steps every time.
acceptance: Given a rule or my choice, then a runbook is attached to the ticket.
Given a step, then it can ask for values in form fields with show / hide / require logic.
Given a step that calls an integration, then it uses only approved integration steps; nothing runs on devices (Q4).
Given progress, then done steps and values are saved on the ticket.

title: Agent logs interactions that may not need a ticket
story: As an agent, I want a light record for each contact, so that first-contact resolution is measured honestly.
acceptance: Given a chat, call or walk-up, then an interaction record is made.
Given a quick answer, then it closes without a ticket.
Given more work is needed, then it becomes an incident or request with the history.

title: Agents work tickets inside Teams or Slack
story: As an agent, I want to work tickets from Teams or Slack, so that I do not switch tools.
acceptance: Given the bot, then I can view, claim, reply, add notes and approve.
Given workflow alerts, approvals or nudges, then the bot messages the right agent or user.
Given my rights, then the bot shows only what I may see.

title: Requester uses two-way SMS
story: As a requester, I want to raise and reply to tickets by SMS, so that I get help without data or apps.
acceptance: Given the company's SMS number (P04), then an SMS creates or updates a ticket.
Given an agent reply, then it goes back by SMS.
Given opt-out words, then SMS stops for that number.

title: Chat gets pre-chat forms, rich messages and proactive prompts
story: As a requester, I want a richer chat, so that I get help faster.
acceptance: Given a pre-chat form, then my details reach the agent first.
Given chat, then buttons, cards and files can be sent and the chat can move to another team.
Given a page or user trigger, then a proactive message can offer help or show an outage notice.
Given the end of a chat, then I can rate it.

title: Admin builds no-code integration steps
story: As a desk admin, I want to call other systems without code, so that fulfilment and rules do real work.
acceptance: Given an integration step, then it has a sequence of HTTP calls with stored, masked credentials, variables, conditions and retries.
Given a response, then values map back into ticket fields.
Given rules, catalogue fulfilment and AI agents, then they can use the steps.
Given an integration, then it has an on / off switch and failures show on Jobs & errors.
Given steps that change identity systems, then they stay off until the founder decision on identity actions.

title: Agent escalates a ticket to Jira, GitHub or Azure DevOps
story: As an agent, I want to send a bug to engineering from the ticket, so that the ticket updates when the fix is done.
acceptance: Given a ticket, then I create a linked issue in Jira, GitHub or Azure DevOps.
Given the link, then status and comments sync both ways.
Given the issue is fixed, then the ticket is updated and the requester can be told.
Given several Jira connections, then each desk picks its own.

title: Desk admin designs ticket lifecycles visually
story: As a desk admin, I want a visual lifecycle editor, so that each desk has the flow it needs.
acceptance: Given the designer, then I drag statuses and allowed moves.
Given a move, then I set required fields and who may make it.
Given desks or ticket types, then each can have its own lifecycle; old tickets keep their version.

title: Desk admin uses more field types and form layout
story: As a desk admin, I want more field types and layout, so that forms capture clean data.
acceptance: Given field types email, number range, phone, URL, dependent list and reference to user, asset or CI, then each validates input.
Given form layout, then sections, separators and columns can be added.
Given these fields, then they work in filters, sort and search.

title: Desk admin creates custom record types
story: As a desk admin, I want our own record types, so that we track things the desk does not know by default.
acceptance: Given a new type (for example key register), then it has fields, forms, lists and permissions.
Given lookups, then it links to tickets, users and assets.
Given rules and reports, then they can use the new type.
Given RLS, then the new records are walled off per company like all desk tables.

title: Audit log streams to the company SIEM
story: As a security admin, I want desk audit events in our SIEM, so that we watch the desk with our other systems.
acceptance: Given syslog, webhook, Sentinel or Splunk, then audit events stream there signed.
Given a failure, then events are kept and retried and shown on Jobs & errors.
Given the stream, then masked values stay masked.

title: Ticket screen changes by type, desk or brand
story: As a desk admin, I want screen layouts per type, desk or brand, so that agents see what matters.
acceptance: Given a layout, then fields, panels and reply templates are chosen per ticket type, desk or brand.
Given no layout, then the default is used.
Given layout changes, then they are audited.

title: Analyst reads desk data in BI tools
story: As a data analyst, I want desk data in Power BI or similar, so that we join it with other data.
acceptance: Given a BI connection, then a read-only dataset with custom fields is available.
Given a schedule, then exports can also be sent to the company storage.
Given rights, then sensitive tickets and masked fields stay out unless allowed.

title: Agent mobile app, help widget and employee centre
Agent works the queue from the mobile app
story: As an agent, I want the desk on my phone, so that I can act away from my desk.
acceptance: Given the app, then I see my queues, reply, add notes, change status and approve.
Given an SLA warning, then I get a push.
Given poor network, then I can draft offline and send later.
Given a manager, then live KPIs and SLA alerts show in the app.

title: Customer embeds the help widget in its site or app
story: As a standalone desk customer, I want our help widget on our website and app, so that customers get help where they are.
acceptance: Given the widget, then it offers KB search, ticket raise and track, chat and bot.
Given a signed-in user, then their identity is passed in a signed token.
Given iOS and Android SDKs, then the same works inside apps.

title: Employee uses one personalised service centre
story: As an employee, I want one place for all desks with my to-dos, so that I find help quickly.
acceptance: Given the centre, then items and articles are shown by my audience.
Given my to-dos, then pending approvals, tasks and surveys are listed.
Given a page builder, then admins set home pages and tiles by role, department or location, including service status and booking.

title: Company runs several brands with their own help centres
story: As a company admin, I want several brands, so that each product line has its own look.
acceptance: Given a brand, then it has its own help centre, domain, support address, theme and templates.
Given one agent team, then they work all brands.
Given themes, then a code-level template can be used.

title: Knowledge quality, audiences and surveys
Knowledge follows KCS quality checks
story: As a knowledge lead, I want article quality scores, so that articles keep improving.
acceptance: Given article states and agent flags, then each article has a quality index.
Given a review, then the reviewer adds coaching notes for the author.
Given reuse counts, then the report shows articles that solve most tickets.

title: Articles are shown by department, location, role or desk
story: As a knowledge lead, I want finer article audiences, so that people see only what applies.
acceptance: Given an article, then its audience can be department, location, role or desk.
Given search and suggestions, then they respect the audience.
Given no audience, then the agent-only / public rule applies.

title: Desk admin builds surveys
story: As a desk admin, I want my own surveys, so that we learn more than one rating.
acceptance: Given a survey, then it has several questions, types (CSAT, NPS, CES) and branching.
Given send rules, then surveys go per desk or item with delay, sampling and throttling per requester.
Given surveys not tied to a ticket, then they can go to a segment.
Given results, then they are cut by agent, team and service and can trigger rules.

title: Agent presence, capacity and shifts
Agents set presence and work is pushed by capacity
story: As a team lead, I want work pushed to free agents, so that load is balanced in real time.
acceptance: Given presence (online, away, busy, offline), then it shows to leads.
Given capacity per channel (for example 3 chats, 10 tickets), then new work goes to the best available agent.
Given an agent at capacity or away, then they get no new pushed work.

title: Lead plans shifts and sees staff forecasts
story: As a team lead, I want shift rosters and forecasts, so that enough people are on duty.
acceptance: Given rosters, then shifts can be set or imported from CSV.
Given the live view, then capacity and load per team show.
Given history, then volume and staff needed are forecast per day.

title: Lead sees availability and productivity reports
story: As a team lead, I want agent time and output reports, so that I coach fairly.
acceptance: Given the report, then time online, away and busy, handle time and replies per hour are shown.
Given time logs, then billable vs non-billable and time vs capacity are shown.
Given cost rates, then cost per ticket is shown.

title: Client contracts and billable time
Account manager records client contracts and prepaid blocks
story: As an account manager, I want client contracts of every type, so that we bill what we agreed.
acceptance: Given contract types (fixed fee, hourly, block of hours or money, per device or user, project), then a client can hold several.
Given billable time, then it draws down the block.
Given a low or used-up balance, then client and account manager are alerted and overage rules apply.

title: Agents log billable time with rates and submit timesheets
story: As an agent, I want billable time with rates, so that clients are billed right.
acceptance: Given a time entry, then it has billable or not, work type and rate.
Given rates by role, client and after-hours, then the right one applies.
Given a weekly timesheet, then a lead approves it before billing.
Given timers, then they can start by themselves when a ticket is opened.

title: Business service catalogue
Service owner publishes business services
story: As a service owner, I want a list of our business services, so that everyone knows what we offer and at what level.
acceptance: Given a service, then it has owner, description, hours, support team, SLA, cost, consumers and status (pipeline, live, retired).
Given requests, incidents and CIs, then they can link to a service.
Given the portfolio view, then investment against value is shown per service.

title: Problem manager runs problem tasks and states
story: As a problem manager, I want tasks and fuller states, so that investigations are organised.
acceptance: Given a problem, then tasks go to several groups with due dates.
Given 'risk accepted' or 'fix deferred', then the problem can rest in that state with a reason.
Given a problem, then it has a priority and a business-impact or cost estimate.

title: Problem manager sees trends that suggest problems
story: As a problem manager, I want trend reports, so that we fix causes before more incidents.
acceptance: Given recurring categories, CIs, resolution codes and alert clusters, then a report flags them.
Given a cluster, then 'create problem' links its incidents.
Given a fixed problem, then incidents avoided after the fix are counted.

title: Requesters see known errors and fix status
story: As a requester, I want to see known issues and when they are fixed, so that I do not chase.
acceptance: Given a published known error, then its workaround shows on the portal and status page.
Given a ticket linked to a bug, then its status shows to the requester.
Given the fix ships, then linked requesters get a notice.

title: Proven low-risk changes are auto-approved
story: As a change manager, I want auto-approval for proven changes, so that CAB time goes to risky work.
acceptance: Given past results per team and model, then a success score is kept.
Given a low risk score, low service criticality and a good success score, then the change is auto-approved.
Given an auto-approval, then the reason is recorded.

title: Pipelines create and gate change records
story: As a developer, I want my pipeline to raise and wait for change approval, so that deploys follow change rules without manual forms.
acceptance: Given GitHub Actions, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Jenkins or similar, then a deploy creates and fills a change record through the API.
Given a standard change, then it approves and closes by policy (tests passed, outside freeze).
Given a normal change, then the pipeline waits until approval.
Given the result, then success or failure is recorded on the change.

title: Change calendar checks CI windows, dependents and busy days
story: As a change manager, I want better clash checks, so that changes do not hit busy times.
acceptance: Given maintenance windows per CI or service, then a change outside them is flagged.
Given CMDB relations, then changes on dependent CIs at the same time are shown as clashes.
Given business events such as payroll day, then changes on those days are flagged.

title: Discovery flags unauthorised changes and drift
story: As a change manager, I want unplanned changes found, so that nothing changes without approval.
acceptance: Given discovery sees new software, hardware or config change with no approved change, then it is flagged for review.
Given a CI baseline, then a drift raises an alert or ticket.
Given a flagged item, then it can be linked to a change or accepted with a reason.

title: Change manager designs a workflow per change model
story: As a change manager, I want a workflow per change model, so that each kind of change follows its own path.
acceptance: Given the designer, then stages (plan, CAB, implement, review) have approvers, tasks, required fields and notices.
Given a template, then it picks its workflow.
Given affected CIs and services, then their owners are added as approvers by themselves.

title: Change tasks follow an order; calendar is shared
story: As a change manager, I want ordered change tasks and a shared calendar, so that work happens in the right order.
acceptance: Given tasks, then each has planned start and end and dependencies.
Given recurring changes, then they are created on a schedule.
Given an iCal feed, then the change calendar shows in Outlook or Google.

title: Standard changes are ordered from a change catalogue
story: As an engineer, I want standard changes as catalogue items, so that safe changes are fast.
acceptance: Given a standard change, then it is published as an orderable item with its form.
Given an order, then the pre-approved workflow starts.
Given access, then only technical staff see the change catalogue.

title: Affected users get planned outage notices
story: As an employee, I want notice of planned outages that affect me, so that I can plan around them.
acceptance: Given an approved change with downtime, then users of affected services (through the CMDB) are told.
Given the change, then a maintenance post goes to the status page and a portal banner.
Given the status page, then each component shows its uptime history.

title: Release manager runs go / no-go checks
story: As a release manager, I want release types and readiness checks, so that we release only when ready.
acceptance: Given release types (major, minor, emergency), then each has phases and milestones.
Given a readiness checklist, then the go / no-go decision is recorded with who decided.
Given Jira or GitHub, then versions and work items are linked.

title: Releases show deployments per environment and code links
story: As a release manager, I want what is deployed where, so that we can trace any version.
acceptance: Given environments (dev, test, staging, prod), then deployments are tracked per environment with version.
Given commits, pull requests and builds, then they show on changes and releases.
Given CIs, then they show the version deployed.

title: Release keeps tests, sign-off, approved versions and notes
story: As a release manager, I want test plans and release notes, so that quality is proven and users know what changed.
acceptance: Given a test plan, then test cases, results, defects and UAT sign-off are kept and linked.
Given approved software versions, then they are kept in a library.
Given release notes, then they publish to the portal or KB.

title: Discovered software is normalised
story: As an asset manager, I want clean software names, so that licence counts are right.
acceptance: Given discovered titles, then they map to publisher, product, version and edition.
Given variants, then they merge by themselves.
Given an admin, then normalisation can be overridden or switched off per item.

title: Devices from many sources are matched with source priority
story: As an IT admin, I want one record per device from all sources, so that the register is trusted.
acceptance: Given osquery, MDM, probe, CSV, cloud and finance sources, then rules match records per CI type by chosen attributes.
Given conflicts, then source priority per field decides, and a duplicate queue shows the rest.
Given import rules, then owner, location or company are set by IP range or host name.
Given gaps (in finance but never seen, seen but not in MDM), then they are reported with a data-quality score.

title: Asset manager reclaims unused licences and seats
story: As an asset manager, I want to reclaim unused licences, so that we do not pay for idle seats.
acceptance: Given licence metrics (user, device, core, concurrent, subscription), then compliance uses the right one.
Given no use for N days, then the seat is proposed for reclaim.
Given reclaim, then it needs approval and the user is told first.

title: IT admin finds and manages SaaS apps
story: As an IT admin, I want a list of SaaS apps in use, so that we control shadow IT and cost.
acceptance: Given SSO sign-in data (Entra, Google, Okta) and expense or invoice imports, then SaaS apps in use are found (read only).
Given each app, then seats, last use per user, vendor, category and renewal are shown.
Given an exit, then the leaver's SaaS seats are listed for removal.
Given a renewal, then an alert suggests seat counts from use.

title: Asset manager keeps stock, consumables and reorder levels
story: As an asset manager, I want stock rooms and consumables, so that we never run out.
acceptance: Given models and stock rooms, then stock levels per model and room are shown.
Given consumables, then they are tracked by quantity and issued against tickets.
Given a reorder level, then a low-stock alert and a draft purchase request are made.
Given transfers, then stock moves between rooms with history.

title: Staff borrow loaner assets
story: As an employee, I want to borrow a laptop or projector, so that I have it when I need it.
acceptance: Given a loaner pool, then I book an item for a period.
Given the due date, then reminders go and overdue items escalate.
Given return, then condition notes are saved and history is kept.

title: Asset manager runs physical verification
story: As an asset manager, I want audits by location, so that the register matches reality.
acceptance: Given a campaign per location, then staff scan tags with the mobile app or employees confirm their assets.
Given results, then a found / missing / unexpected / moved report is made.
Given exceptions, then they can be fixed in bulk with audit.

title: Asset manager disposes assets with certificates
story: As an asset manager, I want a proper disposal flow, so that we follow the law and books are right.
acceptance: Given disposal, then a data-wipe or destruction certificate is required.
Given e-waste, then vendor hand-over and its certificate are kept (India E-Waste Rules).
Given sale or write-off, then the value goes to the depreciation books.

title: Warranty is looked up; certificates and domains are tracked
story: As an asset manager, I want warranty and certificate dates filled in, so that nothing expires by surprise.
acceptance: Given a serial number, then warranty is looked up from the maker (Dell, Lenovo, HP) or marked unknown.
Given TLS certificates and domains, then issuer, expiry and owner are kept.
Given an expiry near, then a renewal ticket is created.

title: Asset shows read-only patch and security status
story: As an IT admin, I want patch and security state on each asset, so that we see risk without remote control.
acceptance: Given osquery and imports from the company's tools, then OS and patch level, encryption, AV and end-of-life OS are shown.
Given a finding, then a ticket or change is created.
Given any fix, then it is done in the company's own tools; YukthiX sends no commands (Q4).

title: Asset manager sees cost of ownership
story: As a finance user, I want cost of ownership per asset and model, so that we buy smarter.
acceptance: Given an asset, then purchase, repairs, contracts, ticket time and depreciation add up to its TCO.
Given a model, then average TCO is shown.
Given a report, then it can be exported.

title: Cloud resources and other inventory tools are imported
story: As an IT admin, I want cloud and other tool data in the register, so that the CMDB is complete.
acceptance: Given AWS, Azure, GCP or VMware read-only keys, then VMs, databases, storage and load balancers import as CIs with tags and cost.
Given Lansweeper, Device42, SCCM or Snipe-IT, then their data can be imported.
Given a schedule, then imports refresh and removed resources are marked.

title: Software policy flags banned software
story: As an IT admin, I want allowed and banned software lists, so that we act on risky software.
acceptance: Given a banned title found by discovery, then an alert and ticket are created.
Given unlicensed software, then it is flagged too.
Given removal, then it is done by the company; YukthiX only reports (Q4).

title: Admin designs the asset object model
story: As an IT admin, I want my own asset types and links, so that the register fits our estate.
acceptance: Given types with inheritance and typed attributes, then I model my assets.
Given references between objects and several schemas, then they are kept.
Given saved queries, then they drive rules, form pickers and reports.
Given ready types (ports, racks, SIMs, phone lines, databases, clusters), then they can be switched on.

title: Employee signs asset hand-over; labels are printed
story: As an asset manager, I want signed hand-overs and printed labels, so that we have proof and tags.
acceptance: Given issue or return, then the employee e-signs a hand-over form with condition photos.
Given label templates, then barcode / QR labels print one at a time or in batches.
Given the signed form, then it is kept on the asset history.

title: IP addresses are managed per subnet
story: As an IT admin, I want IP addresses per subnet, so that there are no clashes.
acceptance: Given subnets, then IPs are allocated to devices.
Given a duplicate IP in a subnet, then it is refused.
Given a subnet, then use is shown.

title: Requester sees and reports on 'My assets'
story: As an employee, I want to see my assets in the portal, so that I report issues against the right device.
acceptance: Given My assets, then I see what is assigned to me.
Given an asset, then I raise an issue or ask for a replacement from it.
Given a check, then I confirm I still hold it.

title: Catalogue requests reserve stock or raise a purchase
story: As a requester, I want to see stock and get a real device, so that requests are fulfilled fast.
acceptance: Given an item tied to a model, then stock is shown.
Given approval, then an in-stock asset is reserved and assigned.
Given no stock, then a purchase order is made and receiving fulfils the request.

title: Services are modelled with a service map
story: As a service owner, I want services mapped to CIs, so that we see which business service is hit.
acceptance: Given business and technical services, then each is a CI with owner, criticality and support team.
Given the map, then it goes from service down to infrastructure.
Given an incident, change or alert, then an affected-service field drives priority, routing and paging.

title: IT admin sees CMDB health
story: As an IT admin, I want a CMDB health dashboard, so that data stays clean.
acceptance: Given CIs, then missing required fields, duplicates, orphans and stale CIs are counted.
Given a problem, then a task goes to the CI owner.
Given trends, then health over time is shown.

title: Dependency maps come from discovery; non-IT assets link to CIs
story: As an IT admin, I want maps built from real data, so that maps are accurate without hand work.
acceptance: Given discovery data on connections, then relations are proposed for the map.
Given a proposal, then the admin accepts or rejects it.
Given non-IT assets, then they can link to CIs and be attached to tickets.

title: Asset manager keeps vendor scorecards
story: As an asset manager, I want vendor scorecards and risk reviews, so that we choose good vendors.
acceptance: Given a vendor, then SLA met %, escalations, tickets, cost and ratings are shown.
Given a risk review, then questionnaire, documents and next review date are kept.
Given review history, then it is kept per vendor.

title: Purchase documents sync to accounting
story: As a finance user, I want POs and invoices in our books, so that no double entry.
acceptance: Given POs, goods receipts and vendor invoices, then they push to Tally, Zoho Books or YukthiX finance with GST fields.
Given a failure, then it shows on Jobs & errors.
Given a sync, then the accounting reference is saved back.

title: Procurement handles limits, quotes and ordering of goods
story: As a buyer, I want fuller procurement, so that spending is controlled.
acceptance: Given approval limits, then POs over a limit need the next approver.
Given price lists and quotes, then they are compared before a PO.
Given invoices, then they are matched to PO and receipt and payment status is shown.
Given goods or services like stationery or catering, then employees order them with tracking.

title: Agent escalates a ticket to a vendor
story: As an agent, I want to work with a vendor from the ticket, so that vendor work is tracked.
acceptance: Given a vendor escalation, then the vendor's case number is saved and the vendor SLA clock starts.
Given email to the vendor, then their replies are parsed back into the ticket.
Given follow-ups, then reminders go until the vendor answers.

title: Contract SLAs give service credits and penalties
story: As a desk admin, I want credits and penalties from contract SLAs, so that contracts are enforced.
acceptance: Given a contract SLA with credits or penalties, then they are calculated per period.
Given a customer or vendor, then the report shows credits owed.
Given a dispute, then notes can be added.

title: Availability and outages
Service owner tracks outages and availability
story: As a service owner, I want outage records and uptime, so that we know and prove availability.
acceptance: Given an outage (full or partial) with start and end, then it links to incidents and changes.
Given availability targets per service, then uptime, MTBF and MTRS are computed.
Given planned maintenance, then it is left out of availability SLAs.
Given outages, then the status page uses them.

title: Service financial management
Finance sets budgets and sees spend
story: As a finance user, I want budgets with spend, so that we stay within budget.
acceptance: Given budgets per period and cost centre, then spend from POs, contracts, tickets and assets is shown.
Given overspend, then an alert goes to the owner.
Given history, then a forecast is shown.

title: Agents add cost lines to tickets and changes
story: As an agent, I want costs on tickets and changes, so that true costs are known.
acceptance: Given a ticket or change, then time cost at a rate, fixed and material costs can be added.
Given costs, then they roll up to budgets and asset TCO.
Given closed tickets, then costs change only by a lead, with audit.

title: Departments get chargeback statements
story: As a finance user, I want service costs charged to departments, so that departments see what they use.
acceptance: Given catalogue and service costs, then they post to the requesting cost centre.
Given a month, then a chargeback or showback statement is made per department.
Given a statement, then it can be exported.

title: Risk register
Risk owner keeps a risk register
story: As a risk owner, I want a risk register linked to services, so that risks are managed.
acceptance: Given a risk, then it has likelihood, impact, owner, treatment and review date.
Given links, then it connects to services, changes, problems, assets and vendors.
Given a review date, then the owner is reminded.

title: Client billing and profitability
Billing runs turn contracts and time into invoices
story: As a billing user, I want invoice batches from contracts and time, so that clients are billed on time.
acceptance: Given a billing run, then contracts, time, expenses and parts become invoice batches.
Given a batch, then it is reviewed and approved before export.
Given Tally, Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Xero, then invoices export or sync.
Given recurring contracts, then recurring invoices are made.

title: Client sees contract balance, time and invoices in the portal
story: As a client admin, I want to see our balance and invoices, so that we trust the bill.
acceptance: Given the portal, then contract balance is shown.
Given time used, then each entry links to its ticket.
Given invoices, then history with line detail is shown.

title: Agents log parts and expenses
story: As an agent, I want to log parts and expenses on tickets, so that they are billed.
acceptance: Given a product, part or expense, then it is logged with cost and sell price.
Given billing, then it is included.
Given stock items, then stock goes down.

title: Owner sees profitability per client
story: As an MSP owner, I want profit per client, contract and agent, so that I price well.
acceptance: Given revenue and cost of time and materials, then profit and effective hourly rate are shown.
Given the dashboard, then unbilled hours, billing status, CSAT and SLA per client are shown.
Given a period, then it can be exported.

title: Ticket archive
Old closed tickets move to a searchable archive
story: As a desk admin, I want old tickets archived, so that the desk stays fast.
acceptance: Given closed tickets older than N months, then they move to a read-only archive on a schedule.
Given search and reports, then archived tickets can still be found.
Given retention rules, then they still apply to the archive.

title: Event rules map, correlate and suppress alerts
story: As an on-call engineer, I want smart event rules, so that I get one incident, not a storm.
acceptance: Given payload fields, then they map to incident fields and CIs.
Given CI topology, then related alerts group under one root alert.
Given classification and severity mapping, then information events do not page.
Given maintenance windows from the change calendar, then alerts are muted.

title: Heartbeat and simple uptime checks raise alerts
story: As an IT lead, I want basic checks without a monitoring tool, so that we hear about downtime.
acceptance: Given a heartbeat, when the ping does not arrive on time, then an alert is raised.
Given HTTP, ping or TLS-expiry checks, then they run from our side and alert on failure.
Given results, then they feed availability.

title: Service health tiles and many alert sources
story: As an IT lead, I want health tiles and more alert sources, so that I see service state at a glance.
acceptance: Given a service, then a tile combines open alerts, incidents and changes.
Given tile state, then it can update the status page.
Given a catalogue of ready alert integrations and email-to-alert, then most tools connect without code.

title: Log anomalies raise alerts
story: As an IT lead, I want alerts on unusual logs, so that we catch problems early.
acceptance: Given logs sent to the desk, then unusual patterns raise alerts.
Given an alert, then it can create an incident.
Given retention, then raw logs are kept only for the set days.

title: IT sees digital experience scores from read-only data
story: As an IT lead, I want device experience scores, so that we fix slow devices before people complain.
acceptance: Given osquery read-only data (boot time, crashes, disk, battery), then each device and department gets a score.
Given a falling score, then a proactive ticket is created.
Given pulse surveys, then employee mood is added.
Given privacy, then no personal files or browsing data are read (Q3).

title: RMM devices and alerts flow into the desk
story: As an IT admin, I want RMM data in the desk, so that all device issues are in one place.
acceptance: Given NinjaOne, Datto RMM or N-able, then devices import as assets.
Given RMM alerts, then they become tickets with the device linked.
Given actions, then they stay in the RMM tool; YukthiX sends no commands (Q4).

title: Capacity trends and plans per service
story: As a capacity manager, I want capacity trends, so that we add capacity in time.
acceptance: Given monitoring metrics, then thresholds and trends per CI or service are shown.
Given a breach of a threshold, then an alert is raised.
Given capacity plans, then they are kept with forecasts.

title: On-call links with PagerDuty, Opsgenie or Squadcast
story: As an on-call engineer, I want our current on-call tool linked, so that we keep it while using the desk.
acceptance: Given a link, then tickets create and resolve alerts there.
Given acknowledgement there, then it syncs back.
Given the link is off, then our own paging is used.

title: On-call overrides come from approved leave
story: As a team lead, I want leave turned into overrides, so that no shift is left empty.
acceptance: Given approved leave in YukthiX HR, then an override is proposed for that shift.
Given a gap in coverage, then the lead is warned before it happens.
Given the override, then it needs the colleague's acceptance.

title: Phone calls ring whoever is on call
story: As a caller, I want one number that reaches on-call, so that urgent issues reach a person.
acceptance: Given the number, then it rings the on-call person now.
Given no answer, then voicemail becomes an alert.
Given escalation, then the next level is called.

title: On-call people set paging rules and see load
story: As an on-call engineer, I want my own paging rules, so that I am paged the way I respond.
acceptance: Given my rules, then I choose channel and delay per step.
Given swaps and follow-the-sun rotations, then they are supported.
Given reports, then pages per person and out-of-hours load are shown.

title: Alerts are acknowledged from Teams or Slack
story: As an on-call engineer, I want to act on alerts in chat, so that I respond faster.
acceptance: Given an alert message, then I acknowledge, escalate or close it there.
Given the action, then the time is recorded for MTTA.
Given my rights, then only allowed actions show.

title: Agents propose major incidents and use a workbench
story: As an incident manager, I want a proposal step and a workbench, so that major incidents are run in order.
acceptance: Given an agent proposal, then a manager accepts or rejects it.
Given the workbench, then it has timeline, task board and child incidents.
Given a communication plan, then audiences, channels and schedule are set.

title: Incident templates set responders and checklists
story: As an incident manager, I want templates per incident type, so that we start fast.
acceptance: Given a type, then responders, channel, bridge, stakeholders and checklist are set in advance.
Given declaration, then the template applies by itself.
Given changes to a template, then they are versioned.

title: Incident timeline is built automatically
story: As an incident manager, I want an automatic timeline, so that the review is easy to write.
acceptance: Given alerts, status changes, chat, pages and recent changes, then they form a timeline.
Given the review, then it starts from the timeline.
Given edits, then the timeline keeps the original entries.

title: One click opens a channel and a bridge
story: As an incident manager, I want a channel and bridge in one click, so that responders gather quickly.
acceptance: Given an incident, then a Teams / Slack channel and Zoom, Teams or Meet bridge are created.
Given responders, then they are invited.
Given the chat, then it is copied back to the ticket.

title: Responders see 'what changed' and swarm with experts
story: As an incident manager, I want recent changes and experts suggested, so that the cause is found fast.
acceptance: Given affected services and CIs, then recent changes, deployments and commits are listed.
Given any ticket, then experts are suggested from past similar tickets and skills.
Given a swarm, then a linked Teams or Slack conversation opens with them.

title: AI drafts resolution notes and hand-over summaries
story: As an agent, I want AI help to solve and write up, so that I save time.
acceptance: Given a ticket, then similar solved tickets, problems and articles are shown with their steps.
Given resolve, then AI drafts resolution notes for me to edit.
Given a reassignment, then a short summary is added.
Given sensitive tickets, then AI uses only data I may see (YX-HD-03).

title: AI helps agents and requesters write
story: As an agent, I want help with tone and wording, so that messages are clear.
acceptance: Given the reply box, then AI can change tone, shorten, expand and fix grammar; my text is kept until I accept.
Given a requester typing a short phrase, then AI suggests a clear description and asks for missing details.
Given AI text, then it is marked as AI-assisted in the audit.

title: Virtual agent completes tasks
story: As an employee, I want the bot to do simple tasks, so that I get things done any time.
acceptance: Given topics, then the bot checks ticket status, raises catalogue requests with form slots and handles approvals.
Given a no-code flow builder, then admins build guided decision trees with API steps.
Given every channel (portal, widget, email, Teams, Slack), then the same topics work.
Given the setting, then the bot can be the first way into the portal with forms as fallback.
Given identity actions (password reset), then they wait for the founder decision.

title: AI answers new emails at once
story: As a requester, I want an instant answer to my email, so that simple issues are solved at once.
acceptance: Given a new email, then AI replies from KB and policies.
Given 'this solved it', then the ticket closes as deflected (YX-HD-04).
Given 'still need help', then it goes to an agent.

title: Admin builds AI agents with guardrails
story: As a desk admin, I want AI agents for repeat work, so that routine steps are done for us.
acceptance: Given the studio, then an AI agent chains steps and approved connector actions.
Given guardrails, then each agent has allowed data, actions and limits.
Given a step that changes data, then a human approves it unless set as safe.

title: Customers sign in to the portal with SSO, a signed token or a second factor
story: As a desk admin, I want customers to sign in the way they already do, so that they do not need one more password.
acceptance: Given SAML, OpenID Connect or social sign-in set up per brand, then customers sign in with it
Given our own site, when it passes a signed token (JWT) for a signed-in user, then the portal and widget trust that identity
Given the setting, then portal users can be asked for a second factor
Given any sign-in, then it is audited and outside contacts stay limited to their own records (YX-SEC-21)

title: Admin schedules bulk actions on tickets
story: As a desk admin, I want actions that run on many tickets at a set time, so that end-of-day sweeps happen by themselves.
acceptance: Given a schedule and a filter, then the action runs on all matching tickets at that time
Given each run, then a trace shows how many changed and the rule-run limits apply

title: Agents see a team feed of record activity
story: As an agent, I want a feed of what my team is doing on records I follow, so that I keep up without opening each one.
acceptance: Given records I follow, then their updates show in my team feed
Given sensitive records, then they never show in a feed for people who cannot see them (YX-HD-03)

title: Desk links GitLab, Linear, Google Chat and cloud-drive files
story: As a desk admin, I want more everyday tools connected, so that agents do not switch apps.
acceptance: Given GitLab or Linear, then escalation and two-way sync work as for GitHub and Jira (SD-2.15)
Given Google Chat, then desk notifications can go there like Teams and Slack
Given Google Drive or OneDrive, then an agent attaches a file or a link from the drive and it is virus-scanned like other files

title: Admin sees API usage and gets alerts near the limit
story: As a company admin, I want to see our API use and be warned early, so that integrations do not stop by surprise.
acceptance: Given API keys, then a dashboard shows calls per key and endpoint over time
Given a threshold, then admins are told when use crosses it (P11 limits apply)

title: Company schedules encrypted backups of its desk data
story: As a company admin, I want scheduled backups, so that I keep my own copy of desk data.
acceptance: Given a schedule (weekly to quarterly), then a full or changed-since-last export is made
Given an export, then it is encrypted with a password the admin sets and the download link expires
Given each backup, then it is audited

title: Customer keeps one ongoing conversation in the messenger across visits and devices
story: As a customer, I want to come back to the same conversation later, so that I never repeat myself or wait on an open page.
acceptance: Given a signed-in or verified customer, then the messenger shows their past conversations and they can continue one on web or in the app
Given the customer has left, when an agent replies, then they get a push notification or an email with the reply and can answer from there into the same conversation
Given a wait, then the messenger shows the expected reply time or queue position and the team's office hours
Given an anonymous visitor who later signs in or gives a verified email, then their conversation joins their contact record
Given consent rules, then no tracking pixel or read receipt is used for the email fallback (M14 D9)

title: Desk admin designs the messenger home and page-aware help
story: As a desk admin, I want a messenger home with the right cards for each page and customer, so that customers find help before they write.
acceptance: Given the messenger, then I arrange its home cards (search, recent conversation, status, articles, news, ask a question) per brand
Given a page address or customer segment, then suggested articles and cards change to match
Given an outage on the status page, then the home shows it first

title: Company sends customer events and builds segments for routing, messages and articles
story: As a desk admin, I want the customer's product activity and segments in the desk, so that agents, rules and content fit each customer.
acceptance: Given the events API, then the company's app sends events such as "signed up" or "payment failed" and they show on the contact timeline
Given contact and account fields and events, then I build saved segments
Given a segment, then it can be used in routing, SLA conditions, proactive messages, surveys and article audiences
Given events, then they follow the company's retention settings and are never sent to AI for sensitive desks

title: Desk sends targeted in-app banners, posts and service notices
story: As a support lead, I want to reach customers before they write, so that known problems and changes do not turn into tickets.
acceptance: Given a segment and pages, then I show a banner, a post or a chat prompt in the messenger or on the company's site
Given an event via API (for example an order is delayed), then a service notice can go to that customer on their preferred channel with P04 preferences and quiet hours respected
Given a message, then reports show how many saw it and how many tickets followed, without tracking pixels (M14 D9)

title: Work is routed by skill, language and priority, and agents pull the next best ticket
story: As a support lead, I want tickets and chats to reach the agent with the right skills first, so that customers get the right answer fast.
acceptance: Given skills and languages on agents and on tickets, then routing picks an available agent with the needed skills and falls back after a set wait
Given an agent clicks "next", then they get the most urgent ticket they are skilled for, ordered by SLA due time and priority
Given routing decisions, then the reason is shown on the ticket

title: More messaging and review channels become tickets
story: As a desk admin, I want LINE, WeChat, WeCom, Arattai, app-store reviews, video comments and fax as sources, so that we answer customers where they are.
acceptance: Given a connected channel, then messages or reviews become tickets and replies go back on the same channel where it allows
Given fax, then it is switched on only when a company asks for it

title: Developers plug any messaging channel into the desk
story: As a developer, I want a channel API, so that a messaging channel we use can feed the desk.
acceptance: Given a registered channel, then inbound messages post to a signed endpoint and become conversations
Given an agent reply, then it is sent to the channel's webhook with retries and a signature
Given the channel, then it shows in the unified inbox like built-in channels

title: Agents answer every messaging channel in one inbox
story: As an agent, I want chat, WhatsApp, SMS, social and other messaging in one live inbox, so that I do not switch screens.
acceptance: Given messaging channels, then live conversations from all of them show in one inbox with the channel marked
Given a conversation, then I can reply on the same channel or move it to email
Given a call dashboard, then call volume, missed calls and wait times show per line

title: Agents take short training courses inside the desk
story: As a team lead, I want lessons and quizzes for agents in a standalone desk, so that new agents learn our way of working.
acceptance: Given a course, then it has lessons from KB articles and a quiz; progress is tracked
Given an HRMS company, then M07 learning is used instead

title: Community gets points, badges and moderated article comments
story: As a community manager, I want points, badges and public comments with moderation, so that helpful customers are recognised and content stays clean.
acceptance: Given helpful posts and accepted answers, then members earn points and badges such as top helper
Given public comments on articles, then they wait for or pass moderation and can be hidden
Given the help centre, then it can be offered in 40+ languages from translated content (US-G-203)

title: Rules use an AI step and AI fills any pick-list field
story: As a desk admin, I want an AI step inside normal rules, so that tickets are classified, summarised or drafted as they arrive.
acceptance: Given a rule, then an AI action can classify, summarise, detect language or intent, or draft, and its output is used by later steps
Given any pick-list field, then AI can suggest its value with a confidence score; below the threshold nothing is set
Given AI is off or has no key or credits, then the step is skipped and the trace says why (M14 Q9)

title: Desk admin imports from Zendesk, Freshdesk, Intercom and Help Scout
story: As a desk admin moving from another tool, I want tickets, contacts, companies and articles imported, so that history is not lost.
acceptance: Given a source, then the same dry run, id references and rollback as other importers apply (US-B-172)
Given a second YukthiX company of ours, then data (not only configuration) can be moved between them with approval

title: Desk links contact enrichment, Google Contacts, email marketing, project, inventory and password-vault tools
story: As a desk admin, I want more business tools linked, so that agents see and share what they need.
acceptance: Given enrichment, then company size, logo and location can be added to contacts from an outside source the company chooses
Given Google Contacts or an email-marketing tool, then contacts sync with consent kept
Given Asana, Trello or similar, then a ticket can create a linked task there
Given an inventory app, then stock levels show on related tickets
Given a password-vault link, then a secret is shared with an agent through the vault and never stored in the ticket
Given the mobile app, then marketplace extensions can show in mobile slots

title: Agent sees and acts on online-shop orders beside the ticket
story: As an agent at an online shop, I want the customer's orders next to the ticket, so that I answer order questions at once.
acceptance: Given Shopify, WooCommerce or another connected shop, then recent orders, items, payment and delivery status show beside the ticket
Given Stripe or another payment tool, then the customer's payments, subscriptions and failed charges show beside the ticket (read only)
Given the right permission, then the agent can refund, cancel or edit an order in the shop with a confirm step, and it is audited
Given the link is off, then stored tokens are deleted

title: AI agent follows written procedures and takes approved actions for customers
story: As a desk admin, I want the AI agent to follow our written steps and call approved actions, so that it resolves order and account questions, not only FAQs.
acceptance: Given a procedure written in plain language with steps, checks and connector actions (for example check order, start a return), then the AI agent follows it in chat, email and the messenger
Given an action that changes data or money, then the customer confirms and the action runs only within limits the admin set; otherwise it hands over to an agent
Given a test set of sample conversations, then the admin runs them before going live and sees each answer, step and source
Given AI-only notes (short facts not shown in the help centre), then the AI agent can use them as sources
Given Q9, then this runs only with the company's own key or YukthiX AI credits

title: AI agent answers phone calls
story: As a desk admin, I want the AI agent to answer simple calls, so that callers do not wait for routine answers.
acceptance: Given telephony is connected, then the AI agent answers from the same content and procedures by voice
Given it cannot help or the caller asks, then the call goes to a person with a transcript and summary
Given recording laws, then callers are told the call is answered by AI and may be recorded

title: Agent asks the AI copilot questions beside the ticket
story: As an agent, I want to ask the copilot how to solve this ticket, so that I get an answer with sources from our articles and past tickets.
acceptance: Given a ticket, when I ask a question, then the copilot answers from internal and public articles and similar solved tickets I may see, with links
Given an answer, then I can insert it into my reply and edit it before sending (YX-AI-01)
Given repeated agent replies, then the copilot suggests a new canned response for a lead to approve

title: Help-centre search shows an AI answer above the results
story: As a customer, I want a direct answer when I search the help centre, so that I do not read several articles.
acceptance: Given a search, then a short AI answer built only from articles I may read shows above the results with links to them
Given low confidence, then no AI answer is shown
Given feedback on the answer, then it counts in the self-service funnel

title: AI reviews every conversation, including the AI agent's, and flags risks
story: As a quality lead, I want every conversation scored and risky ones flagged, so that reviewers spend time where it matters.
acceptance: Given a scorecard, then AI drafts a score for each conversation by people and by the AI agent; reviewers confirm or change it
Given signs of churn risk, escalation, a knowledge gap or a stuck bot loop, then the conversation is flagged for review
Given several reviewers, then calibration sessions compare their scores on the same conversations

title: Support sends consented outbound messages and series to customer segments
story: As a support lead, I want to send onboarding and service messages to segments of customers, so that common questions are answered before they are asked.
acceptance: Given a segment, then I send an email, in-app message, SMS or WhatsApp message, or a series with waits and branches
Given consent and opt-out, then only customers who allow it get non-service messages and every message has an unsubscribe (YX-NTF-14)
Given results, then replies and tickets raised are counted; opens are not tracked (M14 D9)

title: Desk shows in-product tours, tooltips and checklists
story: As a support lead, I want short guided tours inside our product, so that customers learn a feature instead of raising a ticket.
acceptance: Given the messenger script on the company's app, then a tour, tooltip or checklist shows to a segment on a chosen page
Given a tour, then the customer can skip it and it is not shown again
Given content, then it is built from safe templates, no custom JavaScript (ASVS L2)
